newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals called to open lower.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals called to open lower.

text.p: New York precious metals futures were called to open lower Tuesday as the market became uncertain overnight about the consequences of Monday's news of Dutch central bank sales, traders said.
COMEX February gold was called to open off $0.50 to $1.00 from Monday's close. February delivery traded on ACCESS overnight between $359.80 and $357.80 an ounce.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $357.75/$358.25 versus the London morning fix of $357.30.
COMEX silver was called to open 1.00 to 2.00 cents lower.
COMEX warehouse gold stocks Monday were unchanged at 659,671 ounces.
March silver last traded on ACCESS at $4.715, down 0.2 cent from Monday's close.
COMEX silver stocks Friday fell 1,213,859 ounces to 198,229,654 ounces.
NYMEX April platinum was seen opening $1.00 to $2.00 an ounce weaker, while NYMEX March palladium was called to open off $1.00 an ounce.
December's U.S. consumer prices and retail sales figures, forecast to rise 0.3 percent and 0.5 percent respectively, are due at 0830 EST.
December real earnings data are due at 1000.
